title: 2002 AMC 10B Problem 19
statement: Suppose that \(\{a_n\}\) is an arithmetic sequence with \[a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{100} = 100\] and \[a_{101} + a_{102} + \cdots + a_{200} = 200.\] What is the value of \(a_2 - a_1?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(d = a_2 - a_1.\) Then \(a_{k+100} = a_k + 100d,\) so the second block sum is the first plus \(100\cdot 100 d:\) \[ \begin{aligned} &a_{101} + \cdots + a_{200} \\ &= (a_1 + \cdots + a_{100}) \\ &\quad {}+ 10000d. \end{aligned} \]

Therefore \(200 = 100 + 10000d,\) giving \(d = \dfrac{100}{10000} = 0.01.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Each term \(a_{k+100}\) exceeds \(a_k\) by \(100d,\) where \(d = a_2 - a_1\)
Subtract the two block sums to isolate \(10000d\)
